patch_description: The current algorithm independently computes a shortest path from src to every destination and then duplicates the transfer of every partition along every edge of every path. This causes massive redundant transfers: if two destinations share a common prefix of the route, each partition is transferred multiple times over the shared links. A better strategy is to treat the broadcast as a multicast problem: for each partition, build a single directed tree rooted at src that spans all destinations (a Steiner-tree approximation). Data flows once per edge of the tree, and destinations that share upstream links receive data via shared transfer, cutting cost multiplicatively. We use a greedy shortest-path-from-tree heuristic (repeatedly attach the closest un-reached destination to the growing tree via Dijkstra), which is a classic 2-approximation for Steiner trees and dramatically reduces the number of (expensive) inter-cloud edges used. We then record each edge once per partition into the BroadCastTopology, and reconstruct per-destination partition paths by walking the tree so the output format stays compatible. This directly reduces total_cost (the dominant component of the combined score) while keeping the same success guarantees since all edges come from the same feasible graph.
